meta_desc: Solve NCERT Class 12 Determinants Exercise 4.5 on adjoint and inverse of a matrix, with a free 8-question quiz and worked answers to test your prep.

quiz.title: Adjoint & Inverse of a Matrix Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on the ideas behind Exercise 4.5 — adjoint, inverse, singular matrices and the key determinant identities. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: NCERT Class 12 Determinants Exercise 4.5: adjoint and inverse of a matrix

questions.q: For A = [[2, 3], [1, 4]], what is adj A?
questions.explanation: For a 2x2 matrix [[a, b], [c, d]], the adjoint is [[d, -b], [-c, a]] — swap the leading diagonal and negate the other two. So adj A = [[4, -3], [-1, 2]].

questions.q: For any square matrix A of order n, A(adj A) equals:
questions.explanation: The defining property of the adjoint is A(adj A) = (adj A)A = |A| I, where I is the identity matrix of the same order.

questions.q: If A is a 3x3 matrix with |A| = 4, then |adj A| is:
questions.explanation: For an n x n matrix, |adj A| = |A|^(n-1). Here n = 3, so |adj A| = |A|^2 = 4^2 = 16.

questions.q: For a non-singular matrix A, the inverse A inverse is given by:
questions.explanation: A inverse = (1/|A|) adj A, which is written (adj A)/|A|. This is defined only when |A| is not zero.

questions.q: A square matrix A is called singular when:
questions.explanation: A matrix is singular when its determinant is zero. A singular matrix has no inverse, because you cannot divide the adjoint by |A| = 0.

questions.q: If A is a 2x2 matrix with |A| = 3, then |adj A| equals:
questions.explanation: Using |adj A| = |A|^(n-1) with n = 2 gives |adj A| = |A|^1 = 3.

questions.q: For (AB) inverse, where A and B are non-singular of the same order:
questions.explanation: The reversal law gives (AB) inverse = B inverse A inverse. The order flips when you take the inverse of a product.

questions.q: If A is a non-singular 3x3 matrix with |A| = 2, then |A inverse| is:
questions.explanation: Since A(A inverse) = I, taking determinants gives |A| . |A inverse| = 1, so |A inverse| = 1/|A| = 1/2.

faq.q: What does Exercise 4.5 of Class 12 Determinants cover?
faq.a: It deals with the adjoint and inverse of a matrix. You learn to find the adjoint from the cofactor matrix, use the identity A(adj A) = |A| I, and compute the inverse as A inverse = (adj A)/|A| for non-singular matrices.

faq.q: How do you find the adjoint of a matrix?
faq.a: Find the cofactor of every element, arrange the cofactors into the cofactor matrix, then take its transpose. For a 2x2 matrix [[a, b], [c, d]] this shortcut gives adj = [[d, -b], [-c, a]].

faq.q: When does the inverse of a matrix exist?
faq.a: The inverse exists only when the matrix is non-singular, that is when |A| is not zero. If |A| = 0 the matrix is singular and A inverse is not defined, because the formula divides the adjoint by |A|.

faq.q: What is the relation between |adj A| and |A|?
faq.a: For an n x n matrix, |adj A| = |A| raised to the power (n - 1). So for a 3x3 matrix |adj A| = |A|^2, and for a 2x2 matrix |adj A| = |A|.
